what: The heuristic precomputes customer visited/location facts, the depot fact, and a directed routing-cost matrix reconstructed from grounded `visit` and `return-to-depot` operators using their metric costs. It optionally resolves exact `demand`, `capacity`, and `max_vehicles` PNEs, while safely retaining the guaranteed `load` and `vehicles` IDs when present. At evaluation time it identifies the current location and unvisited customers, detects resource-proven dead ends when complete exact resource data is available, computes an MST routing bound over the depot, current location, and remaining customers, and constructs a capacity-aware nearest-neighbour completion including depot restarts and the final return. The returned estimate is 85% of the greedy completion plus 15% of the MST bound.
why: CVRP states are dominated by routing structure, current-route position, and the cost of required depot restarts. The representative instances use metric-like dense customer graphs but vary substantially in capacity and vehicle count, so a pure goal-count heuristic would provide little guidance. The greedy completion estimates actual remaining route cost and reacts to current load when resource PNEs survive translation, while the MST supplies a stable global connectivity signal that reduces sensitivity to individual nearest-neighbour choices. Operator-based cost reconstruction is robust to translation of travel-cost expressions, and optional resource handling ensures the heuristic still works when capacity and demand names have been folded away.
